{{short description|American statistician|bot=PearBOT 5}}
'''Carol Joyce Blumberg''' (died 16 December 2023){{r|obit}} was an American statistician whose professional interests included [[survey methodology]], [[design of experiments]], and [[statistics education]].{{r|auckland}}

==Education and career==
Blumberg earned bachelor's and master's degrees from the [[University of Michigan]] in 1972 and 1974 respectively. She earned a second master's degree at [[Michigan State University]] in 1981, and completed her Ph.D. there in 1982.{{r|auckland}}

Blumberg was a statistics professor at [[Winona State University]] from 1987 to 2006.{{r|winona}} 
After her retirement as a professor emerita at Winona State,{{r|auckland}} she worked for the [[United States Department of Energy]] from 2006 to 2014.{{r|winona}}

She was program chair for the Educational Statistics Special Interest Group (SIG) of the [[American Educational Research Association]] in 1999–2000, and president of SIG in 2000–2001.{{r|sig}}
She also led the  International Statistical Literacy Project of the [[International Association for Statistical Education]] from 2001 to 2006.{{r|iase}}

==Recognition==
Blumberg was chosen to become a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2010 "for notable contributions to statistics education at the national and international level; for outstanding teaching, advising and mentoring; for extensive service to the profession; and for contributions to the  fields of educational statistics and energy statistics".{{r|winona}}
She was also an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]].{{r|isi}}
